name: Speech-Language Pathologist
description: Speech-language pathologists diagnose and treat disorders of speech, language, voice and swallowing — in children who are not talking, in stroke patients who have lost words, in people who cannot safely swallow. ⚠ A median of $97,870 and 17% growth, among the best combinations on this site. ⚠⚠⚠ But the bachelor's is NOT a terminal degree: Florida awards 513 of them a year into 298 master's places, and 89% of the profession holds a master's. This page covers the assistant, the pathologist and the audiologist, because the bachelor's only reaches the first.
credentialNote: ⚠⚠ Three credentials, three levels, and the gap between the first two is a whole degree. THE PATHOLOGIST: all states license speech-language pathologists, and Florida does so under Chapter 468, Part I. The route is a master's from an accredited programme, a supervised CLINICAL FELLOWSHIP after the degree, and a national examination; the ASHA Certificate of Clinical Competence (CCC-SLP) follows the same requirements and satisfies licensure in many states. ⚠ O*NET's respondents are unanimous in a way few occupations are: 89% name a master's and 11% a post-master's certificate — nobody names a bachelor's. THE ASSISTANT: Florida separately licenses the speech-language pathology ASSISTANT under the same chapter and Rule 64B20, and this one IS reachable from a bachelor's — the degree plus at least 24 board-specified semester hours, of which 9 must cover normal human growth and development, psychology and the normal development of speech, hearing and language, with the rest in phonetics, articulation, language disorders, audiometry, screening, therapy or auditory training. ⚠⚠ THE AUDIOLOGIST: a doctor of audiology, typically four years after the bachelor's, and licensure in all states. ⚠ Electronic fingerprinting is required across these professions following Florida's HB 975 in 2024.
bodyHtml:
Three credentials, and the bachelor's only reaches the first

RoleEntry credential2025 medianJobsOutlook 2025–35
Speech-language pathology assistant✅ bachelor's + 24 board-specified hours———
Speech-language pathologist⚠ master's + clinical fellowship$97,870193,400✅✅ 17% much faster
Audiologist⚠⚠ doctorate (AuD)$95,78014,200✅ 11% much faster

✅ The pathologist numbers are among the best on this site — $97,870 with 17% growth and 32,100 new posts over the decade puts it alongside cybersecurity for growth and above it for nothing-else-required stability. O*NET is more conservative on the band (7% or higher) and agrees on direction; the BLS gives the precise 17%.

⚠⚠⚠ The bachelor's is a feeder degree, and Florida's arithmetic proves it

Florida public institutions award 513 bachelor's degrees a year in this field and offer 298 master's places. The bachelor's does not qualify you to practise as a speech-language pathologist — 89% of the occupation holds a master's and O*NET's respondents do not name a bachelor's at all.

⚠⚠ So roughly two bachelor's graduates chase every master's seat in the state, and that is before out-of-state applicants. This is not a reason to avoid the field — it is a reason to treat the undergraduate degree as the first half of a plan rather than as a qualification, and to know the alternative before you need it.

✅ The alternative, and it is the reason this page covers three roles

Florida licenses the speech-language pathology ASSISTANT, and a bachelor's reaches it. Under Chapter 468 Part I and Rule 64B20 you need the degree plus at least 24 board-specified semester hours, including 9 hours covering normal human growth and development, psychology and the normal development of speech, hearing and language, with the remainder in phonetics, articulation, language disorders, audiometry, screening, therapy or auditory training.

⚠⚠⚠ Read that coursework list against a communication sciences and disorders degree and you will notice it is essentially already in it. The 513 Florida graduates a year who do not get a master's place are, in most cases, already close to a licensed job in the field they trained for — and a great many of them do not know it.

⚠ An assistant works under a licensed pathologist's supervision, cannot evaluate or diagnose, and earns considerably less. It is a real career and it is also the best possible position from which to reapply, because it is directly relevant experience.

⚠⚠ You cannot start this major at a state college

Florida carries 315 course numbers in this prefix across just 8 public institutions — FAMU, FAU, FIU, FSU, Santa Fe, UCF, UF and USF. And of those 315 numbers, only TEN are below the 3000 level — of which nine are special-topics, independent-study, co-operative-education or study-abroad shells. Exactly one is a real lower-division course.

⚠⚠⚠ That is the tightest access constraint on any health path on this site. For nursing, radiography or respiratory therapy a student can do two years at a state college and transfer. Here there is nothing to take. Plan an A.A. in general education and transfer into the major at the third year, and choose the general-education courses that the degree will actually want — psychology, statistics, biology and a language course.

⚠ The prefix is also graduate-weighted: 112 of the 315 numbers are at the 6000 level and another 35 above that, against 26 at 3000 and 54 at 4000. That distribution is the profession telling you where it lives.

What the work actually is

O*NET, on speech-language pathologists: evaluate hearing or speech and language test results, barium swallow results, or medical or background information to diagnose and plan treatment; write reports and maintain proper documentation of information, such as client Medicaid or billing records or caseload activities; monitor patients' progress and adjust treatments accordingly; develop or implement treatment plans for problems such as stuttering, delayed language, swallowing disorders; administer hearing or speech and language evaluations, tests, or examinations to patients.

⚠⚠ Note the barium swallow. Dysphagia — disordered swallowing — is a large and growing part of this profession's medical caseload, it carries real risk of aspiration pneumonia, and it is nothing like the speech-therapy-with-children picture most applicants arrive with. The two halves of this career, paediatric language and adult medical, are almost different jobs.

⚠ And the documentation is not incidental — it appears second in O*NET's own task list, because in schools and in hospitals the eligibility determination and the billing record are what fund the therapy.

Necessary skills

  • Phonetics and anatomy, precisely. You are working with a mechanism, and the therapy follows from knowing how it fails.
  • Neurology. Aphasia, apraxia and dysarthria are brain problems, and the adult caseload is largely neurological.
  • Patience across very slow progress, with children and with stroke patients alike.
  • Assessment and documentation. Eligibility, goals and progress data are what justify continued treatment to a school district or an insurer.
  • Working with families, who do most of the practice between sessions and who are often frightened.
  • Comfort with the medical side — swallowing studies, tracheostomies, palliative care. Applicants rarely picture this and it is a substantial share of the jobs.

Advice

⚠⚠ Treat the bachelor's as half a plan. Two graduates for every master's seat in Florida means you should be building a master's application from the first year — research experience, clinical observation hours, and relationships with faculty who will write for you.

⚠⚠⚠ Learn the assistant route NOW, not after a rejection. The licensed SLPA is reachable from the degree you are already taking, and checking the board's 24-hour coursework list against your own transcript while you can still choose electives is the single most useful thing on this page.

⚠ Plan the transfer deliberately. There is no lower-division coursework in this subject in Florida, so do an A.A. that loads the sciences and psychology the major will want, and apply to transfer into one of the seven institutions that teach it.

⚠ Consider audiology honestly. It pays comparably at $95,780 and grows at 11%, but Florida produces 18 AuD graduates a year at two institutions. That is the narrowest route on this site, and it is a four-year doctorate.

And observe both halves of the profession before you commit. A school caseload and a hospital dysphagia round are the same licence and different working lives, and almost nobody applies having seen the second.

cipCodes.note: ⚠ Psychology — 10 Florida public institutions and 6,549 credentials, the largest feeder-shaped degree in the state. Named because the board's assistant-licence coursework explicitly includes psychology and normal human development, and because psychology graduates are common applicants to speech-language pathology master's programmes.

Special education and teaching — 19 Florida public institutions. A genuine adjacent destination: a large share of speech-language pathologists work in schools, and exceptional student education is where the same interest goes when the master's route does not open.
Biological sciences — the anatomy, physiology and neurology this profession rests on, and a common undergraduate route for applicants who decide on the field late.

programs.note: The programme itself — 7 Florida public institutions, 513 bachelor's a year against 298 master's places. ⚠⚠ Read its degrees note before enrolling: the bachelor's is not terminal for this profession, there is essentially no lower-division coursework in the state, and the assistant licence is the bachelor's-level destination most graduates are not told about.

⚠ Not a route to the licence, but a real alternative destination and one many people in this field end up in — schools are among the largest employers of speech-language pathologists, and exceptional student education serves the same interest at 35 Florida institutions against 7.

⚠ Not a route. Named for the structural comparison: both are graduate-entry therapy professions with a licensed assistant tier below them. ⚠⚠ The difference is access — physical therapy's assistant route is a two-year associate degree at 17 institutions, where this one needs a bachelor's plus specified coursework.

courses.reason: Fundamentals of Speech and Hearing Sciences — 3 institutions. The introductory course of the major, and the first one available anywhere in Florida: there is nothing in this subject below the 3000 level.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ Of 315 course numbers in this prefix, only ten are lower-division and nine of those are special-topics or internship shells. ⚠ Plan an A.A. and transfer into the major at the third year — there is no state-college route into this subject.

courses.reason: Anatomy and Physiology of the Speech Mechanism — 3 institutions. The structural foundation: respiration, phonation, resonance and articulation as a mechanism that can be described and measured.

Neural Bases of Speech, Language and Hearing — 4 institutions, the most widely carried upper-division course in the prefix. ⚠ The adult caseload is largely neurological — aphasia, apraxia, dysarthria — and this is where that begins.
Aural Habilitation and Rehabilitation — 3 institutions. Hearing loss and its management, and the bridge between the speech and audiology halves of the field.
Aphasia — 5 institutions, tied for the most widely carried number in the prefix. ⚠ A GRADUATE course, listed to show where this profession actually lives: language loss after stroke and brain injury.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ Graduate level, so it requires admission to a master's programme — which is the step 513 Florida bachelor's graduates a year are competing for against 298 places.

courses.reason: Dysphagia and Communication Disorders — 5 institutions, graduate. ⚠⚠ Swallowing disorders: the medical half of the profession, carrying real aspiration risk, and the part almost no applicant pictures.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ If the medical side is unappealing, find that out before the master's rather than during it — dysphagia is a large share of hospital and skilled-nursing caseloads.

courses.reason: Augmentative and Alternative Communication — 4 institutions, graduate. Communication devices and systems for people who cannot speak, and a fast-moving technical specialism.

Introduction to Psychology — 33 institutions. ⚠⚠ Named explicitly in the Florida board's coursework list for the speech-language pathology ASSISTANT licence, and take it at a state college while you can.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ One of the 24 board-specified semester hours toward the assistant licence. Check the board's list against your transcript while you can still choose electives.

courses.reason: Human Growth and Development — 29 institutions. ⚠ The other subject the board names for the assistant licence: normal human growth and development across the lifespan.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ Nine of the required 24 semester hours must cover normal human growth and development, psychology, and the normal development of speech, hearing and language. This course and PSY2012 are two of the three.

courses.reason: Anatomy and Physiology I — 20 institutions. The structural basis for the speech mechanism course, and the science most transferable from a state college into this major.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Two equivalent packagings: BSC2085 plus BSC2085L at 20 institutions, the combined BSC2085C at 7.

courses.reason: Elementary Statistics — 39 institutions. Required by essentially every master's programme in this field, and the basis for reading the treatment evidence.

Elementary Spanish I — a language course is a genuine professional asset here. ⚠ Assessing language disorder in a bilingual child requires distinguishing disorder from normal second-language development, which is one of the hardest judgements in the field.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ Bilingual speech-language pathologists are in short supply across Florida and the specialism is directly employable. Also a sensible general-education elective while completing an A.A.

courses.reason: English Composition I — 39 institutions. Evaluation reports, eligibility determinations and progress notes are what fund the therapy in both schools and hospitals.
